changed_fields.before: Model of investment timing under uncertainty using real options theory. Source: Dixit & Pindyck (1994), Investment under Uncertainty.
changed_fields.after: Perpetual investment-option benchmark reconstructed from Pindyck (1991), pp.1119-1121, equations5-10, and Dixit/Pindyck (1994), chapter5. Here mu is the risk-neutral drift r minus the opportunity cost of waiting. At default mu=r the opportunity cost is zero: no finite exercise threshold exists, the option-value limit is the asset value, and immediate exercise is never optimal. Trigger_Value is an explicit report label in that case; no infinity or false zero enters integration. Option_Value and its delta are the analytic value-matching/smooth-pasting solution, replacing the unrelated intrinsic-value lag stock. Invested is the current source exercise-policy indicator, not an accumulated construction rate; on the saved strictly increasing deterministic asset scenario it is also irreversible. The existing sinusoidal Noise is a deterministic illustration, not a Wiener process or Monte Carlo GBM simulation. Financial calibration and general path-dependent exercise handling are outside this educational benchmark.

changed_fields.before: Simplified model of viscous pipe flow based on Navier-Stokes equations. Shows pressure-driven flow development, boundary layer growth, and transition between laminar and turbulent regimes based on Reynolds number.
changed_fields.after: Source reconstruction of the single rigid-column momentum balance in Kruisbrink (1996), equation9.66,p.138, with constant boundary head100m, zero valve/minor loss, existing pipe dimensions and kinematic viscosity. Q is volumetric flow, so Q-prime equals area times force/mass. Pressure_Loss is instantaneous Darcy-Weisbach head loss, not head depletion; reservoir storage geometry is not modeled. Smooth-pipe friction follows EPA SWMM Hydraulics (2017), equations7-32/7-33,p.140, with linear transition between Re2000 and4000; zero roughness is the explicit hydraulically smooth idealization already implicit in the former Blasius correlation. The laminar force is evaluated as8*pi*rho*nu*L*V, including its exact zero-flow limit, rather than dividing by zero or flooring Re. Friction_Factor is a report with its undefined-at-rest state explicit. Viscous_Diffusion_Length=sqrt(nu*t) is only a diffusion-scale diagnostic, not a solved boundary-layer thickness. The former capped thickness integrator was unsupported. This educational incompressible, quasi-steady-friction approximation excludes waterhammer and the exact radial Navier-Stokes startup profile.

changed_fields.before: A system dynamics model of nuclear reactor operations based on the point kinetics equations and Stacey (2018) 'Nuclear Reactor Physics' (Wiley, doi:10.1002/9783527812318). Models neutron population dynamics, reactivity feedback, thermal hydraulics, and power control. Reference: UN World Population Prospects. Source: https://population.un.org/
changed_fields.after: Source reconstruction of KTH Nuclear Reactor Dynamics and Stability, chapter3 pp.74-79, Table3-2 and executable Scilab PDModel Example3-2. Four physical states are one-group neutron/precursor densities and fuel/coolant temperatures. All physical coefficients and equilibrium initial conditions are taken from the example. The time origin is shifted to the source reactivity insertion at t=1s: time0 here is immediately after the +0.0022 step; the omitted preceding1s is exact equilibrium.
